title: Sextant extension manifest (sextant-extension.json)
description: Sextant reads this schema itself (crates/sextant-core/src/extensions/schema.rs) and adds checks a schema cannot express: sextantApi must be one Sextant supports, contribution ids are unique per contribution type, and problem rules (sextantApi 2) have unique titles, judge at most 10 kinds, nest `all`/`any` at most 3 deep with 20 conditions per rule, and use field paths (`.a.b`, `[0]`, `["key"]`) that read no Secret values or inline secret fields, at most 5 of them as `{{…}}` placeholders in a message. Metric queries (sextantApi 2) have unique parameter names, use each parameter as a `{{name}}` placeholder (a namespace, name or labelValue only inside a "…" string, a duration only outside strings) and have no comments. Translations (sextantApi 2) name texts this manifest has, keep their limits and, for a problem message, exactly the English placeholders. Rules across objects (sextantApi 3): `missing` is never inside `any` nor about Secrets, and its kind counts among the 10; `newestPer` is a label key. Commands (sextantApi 3) start with a word, every other argument a word or exactly `{{name}}` of a parameter, each parameter used; the target's label selector is `key=value` pairs and its container a DNS label. Section counters (sextantApi 3) are on the extension's own sections (a page of it gives the section a `sectionTitle`), one per section, and count rules its `problems` have. `format` names Sextant's own formats (extension-id, contribution-id, semver, entry-path, identifier, non-blank, json-path); `pattern` says the same as a regular expression for other validators (json-path has none: it is the JSONPath subset of CRD printer columns).

$schema.description: Lets an editor find this schema; Sextant ignores it.

id.description: Unique id: 3–64 characters, lowercase letters, digits, `.` and `-`; starts with a letter or digit, does not end with `.`, no `..`, not a Windows device name (`nul`, `con.x`, `com0`, …).

sextantApi.description: Major version of the extension API the extension is written for; Sextant supports 1 to 4 (2 adds `contributes.problems`, `contributes.metricQueries` and `translations`, 3 adds `contributes.sectionBadges` and `contributes.commands`, 4 adds sources and `not` in problem rules, computed columns, action conditions, `contributes.kinds`, status patches, port-forwards, `contributes.menuItems`, `contributes.services` and `contributes.agentTools`). A newer Sextant keeps reading every version it once read (ADR-0142).

entry.description: The HTML file every view opens, relative to the package root, e.g. index.html or dist/index.html; no part may start with `.`, be `node_modules` (any case), end with `.` or a space, or be a Windows device name.

backend.description: Code that runs outside the window (ADR-0131): a WebAssembly component of the world sextant:extension/backend, the hosts it may call over HTTPS and the credentials the user enters for it. The consent screen shows each host and credential.

module.description: The component, relative to the package root, e.g. backend.wasm.

hosts.description: Host names the backend may call over HTTPS on port 443: lower case, no wildcard, no IP address, not localhost.

credentials.description: Secrets the user enters in Sextant for the backend (an API token, say); only this backend reads them. Ids are unique.

translations.description: Translations of the manifest's texts (sextantApi 2): language tag (`de`, `pt-BR`, `zh-CN`) → text key (`name`, `description`, `pages.<id>.title`, `problems.<id>.message`, …) → text. English is the manifest itself; a text not translated is shown in English. Metric queries, kinds and paths are never translated.

title.description: Text shown to the user: 1–80 characters, not only spaces.

contributionId.description: 1–40 characters: lowercase letters, digits and `-`; unique among contributions of the same type.

icon.description: Name of an icon from Sextant's set (e.g. `workloads`, `customResource`); an unknown name shows the default icon.

order.description: Position among siblings; smaller comes first.

kind.description: A kind without a version: API group (`""` for the core group) and kind, compared ignoring case.

permissions.description: What the extension may do in clusters: clusters × namespaces × kinds × actions, as AI agent access rules.

clusters.description: Clusters by kubeconfig context name: all of them, or only these.

statusPatches.description: Kinds whose status subresource the extension may patch where the rules allow Modify (sextantApi 4): custom resources only.

namespaces.description: All namespaces (and objects without a namespace), or only these namespaces.

confirm.description: Ask the user before every Modify or Delete this rule allows. Default: true.

section.description: A sidebar section of Sextant (`workloads`, `config`, `customResources`, …) or the extension's own.

when.description: Shown only for objects for which this holds (sextantApi 4).
Offered only for objects for which this holds, as a problem rule's condition without `missing` (sextantApi 4).

whyNot.description: Why the action is not offered where `when` does not hold (sextantApi 4).

placement.description: `primary`: a button of the details bar on kinds of the extension's own section (`contributes.kinds`); `more` (default): the "Actions" menu (sextantApi 4).

patch.description: A merge patch Sextant sends itself to each selected object, without the extension's window (sextantApi 4): at most 4 KiB, its only placeholder a whole string value `{{now}}` (the time, RFC 3339).

ask.description: With `patch`: a question Sextant asks before sending it, listing the objects; its texts may hold `{{count}}` and, on an action of one object, `{{kind}}`, `{{namespace}}` and `{{name}}` (sextantApi 4).

headless.description: The action's frame runs out of sight, without a window: it ends with `ui.close` and tells the user with `ui.notify` (sextantApi 4). Not with `patch`.

done.description: With `patch`: what Sextant says once every object got it (sextantApi 4).

jsonPath.description: JSONPath as in CRD printer columns: .spec.size, .status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status, .metadata.labels['app\.kubernetes\.io/name'].

after.description: Title of the column this one goes after; at the end when omitted or unknown.

paths.description: Field paths, the first with a value giving the cell; instead of `jsonPath` (sextantApi 4).

format.description: How the value is shown, sorted and filtered: `text` (default), `number`, `age` (a time), `duration` (from the time to `endPaths` or now), `ratio` (`value/totalPaths`; with the whole there, a missing value is 0, as Kubernetes leaves zero counts out).

endPaths.description: `duration`: the end time, the first with a value; now without one.

totalPaths.description: `ratio`: the whole, the first with a value.

tones.description: A tone per shown value: `ok`, `warning`, `error` or `neutral`.

tooltipPaths.description: The cell's tooltip, the first with a value.

lookup.description: The value picked from a list by an index field (sextantApi 4): `field` of the item of `list` that `index` names (0 when the object leaves the index out); with `nearestBefore`, else of the nearest earlier item that has it; else `orElse`. Before `paths`.

valueText.description: How a `text` or `number` value is written: text with the one placeholder `{{value}}`, such as `{{value}}%` (sextantApi 4).

afterColumn.description: The id of the column this one goes after (`name`, `namespace`, `age`, or one of the extension's own column ids); the same in every language.

cases.description: Texts shown instead of the value where a condition holds, the first that holds.

text.description: Text with up to 5 `{{<field path>}}` placeholders filled from the object; a case whose placeholder has no value does not hold.

value.description: With `format: "number"`: the number the column sorts and filters by while the case holds; the text is still shown (sextantApi 4).

tooltip.description: Shown on hover while the case holds, instead of `tooltipPaths`: text with up to 5 `{{<field path>}}` placeholders (sextantApi 4).

problems.description: Problem rules Sextant evaluates on its own watches (ADR-0137); needs `sextantApi` 2; at most 20 before `sextantApi` 4. Paths must not read a Secret's values or another kind's inline secret fields.

metricQueries.description: Prometheus-compatible queries the extension runs by id with typed parameters (ADR-0138); needs `sextantApi` 2. The extension never sends PromQL.

commands.description: Programs the extension runs by id in a container it names by labels, with typed parameters, never through a shell (ADR-0147); needs `sextantApi` 3. Each is agreed to word for word at install; one that `changes` something is confirmed every time.

kinds.description: Kinds listed in a sidebar section of the extension's own with Sextant's tables, details and actions (sextantApi 4).

section.description: A section of the extension's own: it, a page or another kind of it with this section has a `sectionTitle`.

aliases.description: Short names the command palette takes as a kind prefix (`hr web`).

searchByDefault.description: The command palette searches the kind without being asked to.

printerColumns.description: `false`: the CRD's printer columns are left out of the table (default true).

problemWhen.description: What the table's "Only problems" shows for the kind instead of the objects with an active problem of the rules: those this holds for, a condition without `missing` (sextantApi 4).

menuItems.description: Items of Sextant's menus that open the extension's window (sextantApi 4): `cluster` is a cluster's context menu.

services.description: Services inside a cluster the extension sends requests to through Sextant's own port forward (sextantApi 4), each agreed to at install.

name.description: The Service's name, in the namespace each request names; or `labelSelector`.

labelSelector.description: A label selector picking exactly one Service in the namespace, instead of `name`.

secrets.description: Keys of Secrets of the namespace the service may receive in `{{secret:<name>/<key>}}` or `auth: "secret:<name>/<key>"`, agreed to with it: a Secret by `name`, or every Secret `labelSelector` picks (`service.secrets` lists their names).

port.description: The Service's port: its number or its name.

signIn.description: What the user types to sign in, in Sextant's own dialog (`ui.signIn`): a body value `{{signIn:<field>}}` gets it; the extension never sees it.

secret.description: Hidden while typed (a password, a token).

agentTools.description: Tools for AI agents in Sextant's MCP server, answered by the extension's backend (sextantApi 4); agents get them only when the user turns the extension on in Settings → AI agents.

description.description: What the agent reads to choose the tool.

inputSchema.description: The JSON Schema of the arguments: an object, in a small subset Sextant checks.

sections.description: The extension's own sidebar sections: a title, an icon on the header and a place after one of Sextant's sections (sextantApi 4).

after.description: One of Sextant's sections (`workloads`, `network`, `customResources`, …): this one comes right after it.

clusterSettings.description: A tab of the extension's in a cluster's settings (`view=settings`, contribution `clusterSettings`, the cluster in the context; sextantApi 4).

sectionBadges.description: Counters on the extension's own sidebar sections (ADR-0143); needs `sextantApi` 3. Sextant counts the objects with active problems of the extension's rules and shows the number on the section's header.

section.description: A section of the extension's own: one of its pages with this `section` has a `sectionTitle`.

rules.description: The ids of the problem rules whose problems it counts; left out: every rule.

label.description: Its tooltip and accessible label by CLDR plural form (zero, one, two, few, many, other; `other` given), each with `{{count}}` (sextantApi 4).

fieldPath.description: A field path: `.status.phase`, `.items[0]`, `.metadata.labels["app"]`; no wildcards or filters.

graceMinutes.description: The problem counts only this long after it began (or was first seen).

notify.description: It may send a notification (the default); `false`: listed only.

toldThroughOwner.description: Not told while the object's controller has a problem of this extension's rules (sextantApi 3).

newestPer.description: A label key: of the objects of one namespace with the same value of this label, only the newest can have the problem (sextantApi 3).

group.description: Rules with the same group notify once per object for all of them (sextantApi 4).

notifyAs.description: A field path whose value, when the object has one, is what a notification is about instead of the object (`<kind>/<namespace>/<value>`), so the runs of one owner notify as one (sextantApi 4).

reason.description: The problem's reason, from the object: text with up to 5 `{{<field path>}}` placeholders, as the message (sextantApi 4). Not translated; the title when it comes out empty.

source.description: Which objects of the kind the rule sees (sextantApi 4): those a label selector picks, and only their metadata. Every rule of a kind has the same source.

labelSelector.description: A Kubernetes label selector: `key`, `!key`, `key=value`, `key!=value`, `key in (a,b)`, `key notin (a,b)`, separated by commas.

metadataOnly.description: Only `apiVersion`, `kind` and `metadata` are watched; every path of the rule is then under `.metadata`.

message.description: Text with at most 5 `{{<field path>}}` placeholders.

labelSelector.description: `key=value` pairs separated by commas: the newest ready pod with these labels in the namespace the call names.

argv.description: The program and its arguments: words, or exactly `{{name}}` of a parameter, put in as one whole argument.

changes.description: It changes something: the user confirms it every time. Default `false`.

query.description: PromQL with `{{name}}` placeholders of `params`: a namespace, name or labelValue inside a "…" string, a duration outside strings; no comments.

type.description: namespace: a DNS-1123 label; name: a DNS-1123 subdomain; labelValue: up to 256 characters without control characters; duration: 1m, 2m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 6h, 12h, 1d or 7d.

range.description: The query may also run over a range of up to `maxHours` back; without it, instant queries only.

problemCondition.description: A condition of a problem rule, by `type`; `all` and `any` nest at most 3 deep (4 from sextantApi 4), 20 conditions per rule.

oneOf.description: The object entered the rule's label-selected source less than `minutes` ago, as Sextant saw it; never for objects already there when the list was first read. sextantApi 4; problem rules with a `source.labelSelector` only.

The text at `path` names no object of `kind` in the object's namespace (or, for a kind without namespaces, in the cluster); unknown while that list is not read in full. sextantApi 3; not inside `any`; never a Secret.
The values at `path` and `otherPath` are the same scalar (sextantApi 4).
The value at `path` is a number at least the one at `otherPath`: each a number, a string that reads as one, or a list counted as its length (sextantApi 4).
Holds where `of` does not (sextantApi 4); never around `missing`.
